title: Jon Bon Jovi Cuts MSG Concert Short After Battling Sinus Infection
excerpt: The 64-year-old rock icon ended the penultimate show of his nine-night Madison Square Garden residency after 90 minutes, telling fans he was hurt and promising to reschedule.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jon Bon Jovi ended his MSG concert early due to a sinus infection after 90 minutes.
  • The residency marks Bon Jovi's first live shows since vocal cord surgery in 2022.
  • He promised fans to reschedule the concert and keep their ticket stubs.
  • The final MSG show is scheduled for July 26, with upcoming UK and Ireland dates.

Article summary

Jon Bon Jovi abruptly ended his Madison Square Garden concert on Thursday, July 23, after 90 minutes and 14 songs, telling a sold-out crowd he was battling a sinus infection that left him unable to deliver the performance they deserved.

The 64-year-old rock frontman was performing night eight of a nine-show residency at the iconic New York City venue as part of the band's Forever Tour. After performing the 1986 hit "Livin' on a Prayer" alongside Train frontman Pat Monahan as a guest, Bon Jovi addressed the audience.

"I'm sorry, I'm hurt and you're not getting the best of me. Don't throw away your ticket stubs, I'm gonna figure something out. Just hold onto it, we'll figure out how to reschedule."

— Jon Bon Jovi, addressing the MSG crowd

He added before walking off stage: "But I'm gonna have to cool it for the night. I feel great."

A Comeback Cut Short

The nine sold-out MSG dates represent a milestone in Bon Jovi's career. The band returned to the concert stage on July 7 for the first time since 2022, when their last tour ended and the frontman underwent vocal cord medialization surgery for vocal fold atrophy. At that comeback show, Bon Jovi delivered a nearly two-and-a-half-hour set packed with classics including "You Give Love a Bad Name," "Bad Medicine," and "Born to Be My Baby."

In 2024, the singer told the Sunday Times he might never perform live again if he could not match his earlier standard, saying, "If the singing is not great, if I can't be the guy I once was … then I'm done." But just last month, he told People magazine he was "fully recovered" from the surgery.

"It was longer than I'd ever expected, but it had to be right. We never lost faith," he said.

A representative for Bon Jovi confirmed the reason for the shortened set in a statement to multiple outlets. "Jon Bon Jovi spoke from stage and told fans he has been battling a sinus infection which led to the show's early ending," the statement said, according to Page Six. "Updated information will be available shortly."

Fan Reaction and What's Next

Fans on social media rallied behind the singer. "That must have broke his heart to have to end it early," one concertgoer wrote. Another fan who had traveled from the United Kingdom for the show said they were "still blown away" despite the abbreviated performance, according to Page Six.

Bon Jovi has been joined on the Forever Tour by original band members Tico Torres and David Bryan, along with Hugh McDonald, John Shanks, Phil X, and Everett Bradley. The setlist has drawn from the New Jersey-based band's four decades of hits.

The final date of the MSG residency remains scheduled for Sunday, July 26. Beyond New York, the band's Forever Tour is set to head overseas with dates at Scottish Gas Murrayfield Stadium in Edinburgh on August 28, Croke Park in Dublin on August 30, and three shows at Wembley Stadium in London on September 4, 6, and 9, according to USA Today.

Looking Ahead

Whether the sinus infection will affect remaining tour dates remains to be seen. Bon Jovi's team has not indicated any changes to the final MSG show or the upcoming European leg. For a singer who fought his way back from career-threatening vocal cord surgery, Thursday's setback is a reminder of the physical demands of performing at the highest level — even for a veteran with four decades on stage.

At his first comeback show earlier this month, an emotional Jon Bon Jovi told the 20,000-strong MSG crowd: "I was grateful and humbled by this whole ordeal. Thank you for letting me have this," according to USA Today.
